chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When you enter the Sanctuary, take some idhkhir (a type of aromatic herb) and chew it." And he used to command Umm Farwah to do that. So when one wishes to enter Mecca, let him enter from its upper part if he is entering from the road of Medina. This was narrated.

key_terms.أُمَّ فَرْوَة: Umm Farwah, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.الْإِذْخِر: Idhkhir, a type of aromatic herb used for fragrance and chewing

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette and entry point for entering Mecca according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes chewing idhkhir upon entering the Haram to purify the breath, a practice he also instructed Umm Farwah to follow, reflecting the Shia emphasis on physical and spiritual cleanliness during pilgrimage. Furthermore, he specified that those approaching from Medina should enter Mecca from its upper part, a detail preserved in the chain of transmission from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni's era, highlighting the practical guidance for pilgrims navigating the sacred geography.
